lead.title: Amsterdam's Incision raises €4M from HERAN Partners to take its digital assistant for surgical teams to the US
lead.deck: Founded in 2014 by surgeon Theo Wiggers, Incision makes Assist, which gives OR staff procedure-, role- and surgeon-specific guidance (instruments, materials, room set-up), plus MySPD for sterile processing and Incision Academy for training; its platforms run in about 300 hospitals across more than 20 countries. The third investment from HERAN HealthTech Fund II, whose partner Mercedes Tuin joins the supervisory board, the round will fund US expansion (a market entered in 2022), partnerships with device makers and platform development: user hospitals report 15% faster room turnover and 14% fewer intraoperative door movements.

milestone.title: NHS England hands CGI £47.7M to build the foundations of England's Single Patient Record
milestone.summary: The UK arm of the Canadian group will build the patient-level datastore, ingestion pipelines, APIs, authorisation and audit, integrate with the National Care Records Service, and develop Clinician360 for clinicians, then Patient360 via the NHS App; first care pathways: maternity and frailty. The 12-month contract started on November 2 and can be extended by a year.
milestone.why: It is the first major building block of the single record promised by the NHS 10 Year Health Plan, which aims to give clinicians access to the history of at least 80% of patients by April 2027. NHS England says several suppliers will be involved, with more contracts over two years: an opening for interoperability and clinical-app vendors able to plug into this layer.

deal.thesis: Dutch group Wolters Kluwer Health pays $40M in cash and up to $60M in performance-based earn-outs for the Californian maker of EHR-embedded clinical decision support (Pathways, and eCART, a 510(k)-cleared deterioration-detection engine): about 5.7x expected year-end 2026 ARR ($7M) upfront, 14.3x at most. Two lessons for VCs: clinical-content giants (UpToDate Expert AI, adopted by 2,700+ US hospitals) now buy workflow distribution rather than build it, and earn-outs are becoming the norm to bridge valuations and revenue.

brefsEurope.title: MPAssist, a Swiss AI documentation assistant founded in 2024, breaks even without raising capital
brefsEurope.summary: Founded by Michelle Plüss and Enrico Mayor, the startup automates reports, nursing documentation and patient-record summaries for 170+ Swiss healthcare institutions and has beaten its CHF 500,000 revenue target. The CHF 500,000-for-20% offer made on 'Die Höhle der Löwen' was not finalised, as the parties disagreed on long-term strategy.

brefsEurope.title: NHS England taps the Royal College of Radiologists to design national monitoring of deployed diagnostic AI
brefsEurope.summary: A five-month contract (almost £230,000 incl. VAT, starting November 26) to define how to track real-world performance, model drift and bias of AI tools, especially in cancer screening, and whether to procure a dedicated platform. A future market for AI-monitoring vendors.

brefsEurope.title: Heidi ambient AI pilot in Leeds: 91% of patients say clinicians were more focused
brefsEurope.summary: At the Leeds Gender Identity Service, where 72.7% of staff reported a negative impact from admin, Heidi Health's ambient scribe was piloted; 91% of service users found clinicians more focused. The trust is now consulting service users on AI in its community services, open until January 2027.

brefsIntl.title: XpertDox raises $20M Series A led by Savant Growth for neuro-symbolic AI medical coding
brefsIntl.summary: XpertCoding turns unstructured EHR documentation into billing codes for 40+ organisations, including seven major community health centres; Kennet Partners participates. Autonomous coding remains one of the fastest-paying AI use cases for thin-margin providers.

brefsIntl.title: The VA and the Department of War connect to Oracle Health's exchange network under TEFCA
brefsIntl.summary: Since November 5, military and veterans' clinicians can query civilian hospitals' and clinics' records through a single connection point and reconcile them into the primary chart; imaging and medication histories will follow. A large-scale public-private exchange precedent worth watching for the EHDS.

brefsIntl.title: Redesign Health launches a growth equity practice, Series A to pre-IPO, in healthcare AI
brefsIntl.summary: The New York venture builder, with Richie Chaikof leading the effort, will back health IT, AI-enabled services and clinical AI companies; fund and cheque sizes undisclosed. One more buyer for health-AI scale-ups, including European ones targeting the US.

word.definition: Continuous, real-world, site-by-site tracking of how a medical AI tool already in use is performing, to catch in time a drop in reliability, data drift or bias against certain patients.

parts.label: Output capture
parts.role: continuously collect the AI's predictions (via API, HL7 or DICOM) and, when available, clinical ground truth

parts.label: Metrics and alerts
parts.role: track performance, data drift and subgroup gaps, and alert on degradation

parts.label: Governance
parts.role: the decision loop (radiologists, AI committee, manufacturer, regulator) that fixes, retrains or withdraws the tool

how.t: The monitoring platform plugs into the deployed AI's outputs and hospital data, ideally without data leaving the site (federated approach).
It computes clinical metrics in near real time (agreement with the radiologist, alert rates, subgroup performance) and detects drift.
When something is off (imaging artefacts, automation bias, a sensitivity drop), teams and the manufacturer are alerted to fix or pause the tool, and the report feeds vigilance.

word.why: Regulators are moving from one-off approval to whole-lifecycle oversight: the MHRA adopted all 44 recommendations of a commission that found one-off assessments insufficient, the FDA asks for performance-monitoring plans, and the NHS is designing a national scheme. A vendor-neutral, hospital-bought, recurring software layer is forming between hundreds of cleared AI tools and their users: a nascent market where Europe already has pioneers.

startups.name: Aival
startups.use: Aival Monitor alerts hospitals when a deployed AI product loses performance (data drift) and breaks results down by subgroup; listed in the UK government's AI assurance portfolio

startups.name: Newton's Tree
startups.use: Vendor-neutral hospital platform for selecting, evaluating and monitoring AI; its federated FAMOS service monitored chest X-ray AI (Annalise.ai, Qure.ai) in real time at Leeds Teaching Hospitals

startups.name: deepc
startups.use: Radiology AI orchestration platform (deepcOS) that publishes a post-deployment governance framework built on technical performance, algorithm stability and clinical use
